title: PingKit Agent
name: pingkit-agent
description: Watches your own network from a Linux host that stays on and alerts PingKit on your iPhone when the internet goes down, a new device joins or a device goes offline. Source: https://github.com/pingkit/agent
note: Before you deploy, open PingKit on your iPhone, go to Agents, tap Add an Agent and keep the 8-character code it shows; it works once, for 10 minutes. After the stack starts, open http://<your-host>:7474/ and type the code on the status page. The iPhone connects on port 7475. Host networking is the one privilege, and it is required: the agent reads the host's neighbour (ARP) table and hears mDNS and SSDP from your devices, which a bridge network hides. Every capability is dropped, the root file system is read-only and it runs as user 65532. If your Portainer admin blocks host networking for regular users, an admin has to deploy it. Linux hosts only: Docker Desktop on Windows or macOS cannot see your devices. State lives in the pingkit-agent-data volume. Docs: pingkit.app/agent/docker
